Sergio / Ben — I reviewed Maria’s PO and drafted redlines to the order form focused on three commercial risk items. Summary below; full redline attached (OF_redline_v2.docx).

1) Net terms / payment trigger
- Redline: Net45 accepted; include clause that invoices become payable upon delivery of invoice to the invoicing email and acceptance that invoice is final unless disputed within 14 days. Adds standard late fee language.

2) Invoice recipient entity
- Redline: Allow SplitPay to nominate invoicing entity per Exhibit A. Add requirement to provide a PO / formal remit instructions at contract signature. This prevents mid-term swaps without written consent.

3) VAT / reverse-charge handling + evidence
- Redline: Customer must provide VAT registration number and a signed VAT residency statement prior to first invoice if reverse-charge is to apply. If evidence is not provided, Redwood will invoice VAT and customer will be responsible for reclaiming.
- Request: If SplitPay expects continuous reverse-charge across EU entities, we need a one-page spreadsheet listing entities, VAT IDs, and supporting docs (redline_summary.xlsx).

4) Minimum commit / true-up
- Redline: Minimum commit (first 3 months) and true-up window (30 days) — propose a 3-month minimum covering baseline provisioning costs, with monthly true-up reconciliations. This is softer than a full-year mincommit but protects capacity allocation for the pilot.

5) Escrow / invoice dispute escalation
- Add a short escalation path: Procurement -> AE -> Finance -> Legal with 5 business day SLA for initial acknowledgement.

Please review the attached docx redline and the summary spreadsheet for tax evidence we’ll request from the customer. If Ben agrees on the soft mincommit wording we can send the redline to Maria tomorrow with an ASK to return tax evidence and entity mapping.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
